What We Do

Full-Service Geriatric Medicine Revenue Cycle Management

Geriatric billing combines high-complexity E/M coding, chronic care management monthly cycles, annual wellness visit coordination, and transitional care management after hospital discharge. PMEX manages every revenue stream so geriatric practices capture everything they have earned.

Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment

99205 or 99215 coded from the full geriatric evaluation at correct complexity.

Chronic Care Management

CCM (99490, 99487) billed monthly with consent documentation tracked per patient.

Annual Wellness Visit

G0438 (initial) and G0439 (subsequent) billed separately from sick visits.

Transitional Care Management

TCM (99495, 99496) billed after hospital, SNF, or rehab discharge with correct timing.

Advance Care Planning

ACP (99497, 99498) billed when separately documented from the E/M visit.

Nursing Home and SNF Visits

Nursing facility E/M codes (99304-99310) billed correctly by care setting.

Common Geriatric Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Annual wellness visit billed as a standard office visit, triggering patient cost-sharing incorrectly.

PMEX applies G0438 or G0439 for AWVs and confirms the visit type before submission to protect patient benefit.

CCM billed without written patient consent documented in the chart.

PMEX tracks CCM consent per patient and confirms it is on file before the first CCM claim each enrollment period.

Transitional care management not billed after hospital or SNF discharge.

PMEX flags every discharge and confirms 99495 or 99496 eligibility within the required billing window.

Complex geriatric E/M coded at low complexity when MDM supports high complexity.

PMEX codes from 2021 MDM criteria and captures the full complexity of multi-problem geriatric encounters.

CCM time not fully documented, falling short of the 20-minute monthly threshold.

PMEX tracks documented CCM minutes per patient per month and bills only when the threshold is confirmed met.

Home visit E/M codes (99341-99350) used when domiciliary codes (99334-99340) apply.

PMEX confirms the care setting before applying the correct E/M code series for each visit type.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Geriatric Billing

Geriatric practices lose 15 to 24 percent of revenue to AWV miscoding, CCM documentation gaps, and TCM timing errors.

PATTERN 01

AWV Billed Same Day as Problem Visit Without Correct Coding

Patient presents for AWV and physician addresses a new problem in the same visit. Only G0439 submitted. The problem-focused E/M (99213 with modifier 25) never billed. Revenue for the separate problem visit lost.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX identifies same-day AWV plus problem visits and submits the E/M separately with modifier 25, confirmed against the documentation that a separately identifiable problem-focused service was provided.

PATTERN 02

TCM Not Billed After Hospital Discharge

Patient discharged from hospital. Practice completes the required follow-up within 14 days. No one submits 99495 (moderate complexity TCM, $165). The 30-day billing window closes. Revenue permanently lost.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks every hospital, SNF, and rehab discharge and flags the TCM billing window per patient. 99495 or 99496 is submitted as soon as the required contact and face-to-face visit are documented.

PATTERN 03

CCM Billed Without Monthly Time Documentation

CCM (99490) submitted for a patient. Payer requests documentation of 20 minutes of clinical staff time. Time was not logged in the EHR. Claim denied. Prior months at risk for audit.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX confirms documented CCM minutes in the clinical system before billing each monthly cycle. Months where time documentation falls short are not billed until time is properly recorded.
